l: man, Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar), Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar)
s: Man is questioned about what made him careless concerning his Lord. He was created, fashioned, proportioned, and cast into whatever form He willed.

l: Judgment, Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar), Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar)
s: The Judgment is denied by some. On its day, each soul will face the consequences of what it sent before and left behind.

l: guardians, Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar), Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar)
s: Guardians are above man, generous and recording, and they know all that people do.

l: righteous, Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar), Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar)
s: The righteous will be in delight.

l: wicked, Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar), Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar)
s: The wicked will be in hell and will burn there on the Day of Judgment. They will not be absent from it.

l: hell, Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar), Surah 82: The Cleaving (Al-Infitaar)
s: Hell is where the wicked will be, burning on the Day of Judgment, and they will not be absent from it.

l: Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: The unit condemns the defrauders, who demand full measure for themselves but cause others loss. It warns that mankind will be raised on the Awful Day to stand before Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, and that the repudiators of the Day of Judgment will face punishment in hell. It contrasts the guilty, who mock those who believed, with the righteous, who enjoy delight and drink from Tasnim. On that day, those who believed will have the laugh of disbelievers.

l: the defrauders, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: They demand full measure when taking from mankind, but when measuring or weighing for others, they cause them loss. They are warned of an Awful Day when they will be raised and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.
They will be raised again on the Awful Day and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.

l: the Awful Day, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: It is the day when mankind will be raised and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.

l: Allah (Lord of the Worlds), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: Mankind will stand before Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, on the Awful Day. The righteous are brought near unto their Lord.

l: the resurrection, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: The text warns that the defrauders will be raised again and stand before the Lord of the Worlds.

l: the repudiators, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: They deny the Day of Judgment and are called criminal transgressors. Their record is in Sijjin, they will be covered from the mercy of their Lord, and they will burn in hell.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: The repudiators deny it, and none denies it save each criminal transgressor.
The repudiators will burn in hell, where they will be told that it is what they used to deny.

l: the righteous, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: Their record is in Illiyin, a written record attested by those brought near unto their Lord. They are in delight, reclining on couches and receiving pure wine mixed with water from Tasnim.
The righteous are in delight, whose radiance is visible in their faces. They receive a pure, sealed wine and drink from Tasnim.

l: the guilty, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: They used to laugh at those who believed, wink at one another when passing them, return to their own folk jesting, and say that those who believed had gone astray.

l: those who believed, Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin), Surah 83: Defrauding (Al-Mutaffifin)
s: They were mocked by the guilty, but on the appointed day they will have the laugh of disbelievers while reclining on high couches and gazing.
The guilty used to laugh at those who believed, but on that day those who believed will have the laugh of disbelievers.

l: Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj) concerns the owners of the ditch who persecuted believers by witnessing them in a fuel-fed fire. It condemns those who persecute believing men and women without repentance and promises them hell, while promising believers who do good works Gardens beneath which rivers flow. It describes Allah as the Sovereign, Witness, Forgiving, Loving, and Doer of what He wills, and mentions the hosts of Pharaoh and Thamud. It declares that the Qur'an is glorious and kept on a guarded tablet.

l: Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: It recounts the destruction of the owners of the ditch and their persecution of believers. It also describes the fate of persecutors and the reward of believers who do good works.

l: Allah, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: Allah is described as the Mighty, the Owner of Praise, the Sovereign of the heavens and the earth, and the Witness of all things. He is also described as Forgiving, Loving, Lord of the Throne of Glory, and Doer of what He wills.

l: owners of the ditch, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: The owners of the ditch sat by a fuel-fed fire and witnessed what they did to the believers. They were self-destroyed because they persecuted believers who had naught against them except that they believed in Allah.

l: fire, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: The fire was fuel-fed, and the owners of the ditch sat by it while witnessing what they did to the believers.

l: believers, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: The believers were persecuted by the owners of the ditch because they believed in Allah. Those who believe and do good works are promised Gardens beneath which rivers flow.

l: persecutors of believers, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: Persecutors of believing men and believing women are warned that, if they do not repent, they will face the doom of hell and the doom of burning.

l: hell, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: Hell is the promised fate of those who persecute believing men and believing women and do not repent.

l: Gardens, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: Gardens beneath which rivers flow are promised to those who believe and do good works. They are described as the Great Success.

l: punishment of Allah, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: The punishment of Allah is described as stern.

l: Qur'an, Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj), Surah 85: The Constellations (Al-Burooj)
s: The Qur'an is described as glorious and as being on a guarded tablet.

l: Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq) concerns the Morning Star, human creation, resurrection, and the Qur'an. It says that every human soul has a guardian and that hidden thoughts will be searched out. It declares the Qur'an to be a conclusive word and describes a plot against Muhammad. The disbelievers are to be given a respite and dealt with gently for a while.

l: Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: It concerns the Morning Star, human creation, resurrection, the Qur'an, Muhammad, and the disbelievers. It declares that the Qur'an is a conclusive word and describes a plot against Muhammad.

l: Morning Star, Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: It is described as a piercing Star. The text asks what will tell about the Morning Star and swears by it.

l: Qur'an, Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: It is described as a conclusive word and not a pleasantry.

l: Muhammad, Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: A plot is made against him by the disbelievers, and he is told to give them a respite and deal gently with them for a while.

l: disbelievers, Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq), Surah 86: The Morning Star (At-Taariq)
s: They plot a plot against Muhammad. They are to be given a respite and dealt with gently for a while.

l: Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa) concerns praise of the Lord the Most High, who creates, measures, guides, brings forth pasturage, and turns it to stubble. It states that Allah knows what is disclosed and hidden, and that the way to ease will be made accessible. The passage urges reminding people, describing the heedful as successful and the hapless as flung into the great Fire. It teaches that the Hereafter is better and more lasting than the life of the world and says this is found in the former scrolls, the Books of Abraham and Moses.

l: Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: It praises the Lord the Most High and urges remembrance, prayer, and reminding. It teaches that the successful person grows, remembers the name of the Lord, and prays, while the hapless flouts the reminder and is flung to the great Fire.

l: Allah (Lord the Most High), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: Allah is described as the Lord the Most High, who creates, disposes, measures, guides, brings forth pasturage, and turns it to russet stubble. Allah knows what is disclosed and what remains hidden, and wills what is excepted from being forgotten.

l: the great Fire, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The great Fire is the place to which the most hapless person will be flung. In it, he will neither die nor live.

l: the life of the world, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The life of the world is preferred by some over the Hereafter. It is described as inferior to and less lasting than the Hereafter.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The Hereafter is described as better and more lasting than the life of the world.

l: the Books of Abraham and Moses, Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa), Surah 87: The Most High (Al-A'laa)
s: The Books of Abraham and Moses are identified as the former scrolls in which this teaching is found.

The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia) describes the event that will shake the earth, grind the hills to dust, and divide people into three groups. Those brought nigh and those on the right hand receive gardens, nourishment, peace, and delight, while those on the left hand, including the erring deniers and rejecters, face scorching wind, boiling water, the tree called Zaqqum, and hell-fire. The text calls human beings to recognize that the Lord of the Worlds creates them, controls death, cultivates plants, sends water, and causes fire. It declares the noble Qur'an to be a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, kept in a hidden Book, and calls Muhammad to praise the name of his Lord.
The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia) concerns the event, the division of people into three groups, their respective outcomes, and signs of the Lord of the Worlds' power.
The event will befall without denial, abase some, exalt others, shake the earth, and reduce the hills to scattered dust.
The earth will be shaken with a shock when the event befalls.

l: those on the right hand, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: Those on the right hand receive gardens, shade, flowing water, abundant fruit, raised couches, and peace. They include a multitude of those of old and a multitude of those of later time.

l: those on the left hand, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: Those on the left hand are in scorching wind, scalding water, and black smoke. They persisted in awful sin and will face a terrible welcome on the Day of Judgment.

l: the foremost in the race, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The foremost in the race are brought nigh and receive gardens of delight. They include a multitude of those of old and a few of those of later time.

l: those brought nigh, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: Those brought nigh receive breath of life, plenty, and a Garden of delight.

l: the gardens of delight, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The gardens of delight contain couches, immortal youths serving bowls and cups, preferred fruit, desired fowl, fair ones, and peace. They are a reward for what people used to do.

l: the tree called Zaqqum, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The tree called Zaqqum will be eaten by the erring deniers, who will fill their bellies with it.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The Day of Judgment is when the erring deniers receive their welcome of boiling water and roasting at hell-fire.

l: the appointed day, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The appointed day is the tryst to which those of old and those of later time will all be brought together.
Human beings are created by the Lord of the Worlds and are questioned about what they emit, cultivate, drink, and use to make fire. They are urged to admit the truth and give thanks.
Death is meted out among human beings, and the Lord of the Worlds cannot be outrun.

l: the first creation, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The first creation is known to human beings and is presented as a reason for them to reflect.
Water is drunk by human beings and comes from rainclouds by the Lord of the Worlds' causing. If He willed, He could make it bitter.
Fire is struck out by human beings, but the Lord of the Worlds causes its tree to grow. He appointed it a memorial and a comfort for dwellers in the wilderness.

l: the noble Qur'an, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The noble Qur'an is described as a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds. The text asks whether people scorn this Statement and make denial of it their livelihood.

l: the hidden Book, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The noble Qur'an is in a Book kept hidden, which none touches save the purified.

l: the Lord of the Worlds, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The Lord of the Worlds creates human beings, sends revelation, controls death, cultivates plants, sends water, causes fire, and is called Tremendous.
Muhammad is told to say that those of old and those of later time will be brought together, and to praise the name of his Lord, the Tremendous.

l: the soul of the dying person, Surah 56: The Inevitable (Al-Waaqia)
s: The soul of the dying person comes up to the throat while people look on. The Lord of the Worlds is nearer to it than they are, though they do not see.
The rejecters, who are erring, receive boiling water and roasting at hell-fire.
Hell-fire is the place of roasting that welcomes the rejecters and the erring.

This unit concerns Allah's hearing and judgment, the pleading woman, Muhammad, and rulings about wives who are repudiated by comparison to mothers. It addresses secret conferences, conspiracy, alms before conference with Allah's messenger, oaths, and relations with those opposed to Allah and His messenger. It describes the fate of disbelievers and the devil's party, and the success of believers and Allah's party. It also describes the Day of Resurrection, Hell, the Fire, and the Gardens.

Allah hears the pleading woman’s complaint and the believers’ conversations, knows all things, and witnesses all things. Allah sets penalties and commands, forgives, prepares punishment and reward, and decrees that He and His messengers will conquer.

l: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila), Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: The Pleading Woman is the woman who disputes with Muhammad concerning her husband and complains to Allah. Allah hears her saying.
Muhammad is addressed by the pleading woman concerning her husband. People hold conferences with him, and he is instructed to require alms before such conferences.

l: the pleading woman, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: The pleading woman disputes with Muhammad concerning her husband and complains to Allah. Allah hears her colloquy.

Wives are wrongfully treated as mothers when their husbands make that comparison. A husband who retracts such a statement must free a slave, fast for two successive months, or feed sixty needy ones according to his ability.

l: Allah's messenger, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: Allah's messenger is opposed by some, and disobedience toward him is condemned. Believers are told to conspire for righteousness and piety and to obey Allah and His messenger.
Disbelievers face a painful doom and a shameful doom. The limits imposed by Allah are described as applying against them.

Believers are told to avoid conspiracies for crime, wrongdoing, and disobedience, and to pursue righteousness and piety. Allah will exalt those who believe and have knowledge to high ranks, and believers are told to put their trust in Allah.

l: the devil, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: The devil causes conspiracy so that believers are vexed, though he cannot harm them except by Allah’s leave. The devil engrosses those who follow him and causes them to forget remembrance of Allah.

l: the devil's party, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: The devil's party forgets remembrance of Allah and will be among the losers.

l: Allah's party, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: Allah's party consists of those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and do not love those who oppose Allah and His messenger. Allah writes faith upon their hearts, strengthens them with a Spirit from Him, and brings them into Gardens where they abide.

l: those who oppose Allah and His messenger, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: Those who oppose Allah and His messenger are abased, will be among the lowest, and face a shameful or dreadful doom. Believers are not to love them even when they are fathers, sons, brothers, or clan.

l: Day of Resurrection, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah raises people together and informs them of what they did. Their forgotten deeds are accounted for, and they swear to Allah as they swear to people while imagining they have some standing.
Hell suffices those who greet Muhammad with a greeting Allah did not give and question why Allah should punish them. They will feel its heat, and it is described as a hapless journey's end.
The Fire is the abode of those whose wealth and children avail them nothing against Allah. They will abide therein.
The Gardens have rivers flowing underneath them. Allah's party will enter them and abide therein, with Allah well pleased with them and they well pleased with Him.

Some people swear false oaths knowingly and use their oaths as a shelter to turn others from Allah's way. On the Day of Resurrection, they will swear to Allah as they swear to people and will be exposed as liars.

Conspiracy is forbidden when directed toward crime, wrongdoing, or disobedience toward Allah's messenger. Conspiracy is attributed to the devil as a means of vexing believers, while believers are instructed to conspire for righteousness and piety.
Alms are to be offered before holding conference with Allah's messenger because that is better and purer. Those unable to provide alms are excused, and Allah forgives those who do not do so.
Faith is written upon the hearts of those who do not love people opposing Allah and His messenger. Allah strengthens them with a Spirit from Him.

l: shameful doom, Surah 58: The Pleading Woman (Al-Mujaadila)
s: A shameful doom is prepared for those who oppose Allah and His messenger and for those who use oaths to turn people from Allah's way.

This unit concerns Allah, the People of the Scripture who disbelieved, the believers, the fugitives, and the hypocrites. It describes the first exile, the distribution of spoil, the loyalty and generosity of the believers, and the promises and failures of the hypocrites. It warns of punishment in the Fire and contrasts the owners of the Fire with the owners of the Garden. It glorifies Allah by recounting His names and attributes and teaches that the Qur'an would humble a mountain through fear of Allah.

Allah is glorified by all that is in the heavens and earth and is described as Mighty, Wise, Beneficent, Merciful, Sovereign Lord, Holy One, Peace, Keeper of Faith, Guardian, Majestic, Compeller, Superb, Creator, Shaper out of naught, and Fashioner. Allah caused the People of the Scripture who disbelieved to go forth, gave spoil to His messenger, and is stern in reprisal against those opposed to Him.

l: Surah 59: The Exile (Al-Hashr), Surah 59: The Exile (Al-Hashr)
s: Surah 59: The Exile (Al-Hashr) is revealed at Medina and recounts the first exile, the treatment of spoil, the conduct of believers and hypocrites, and the glorification of Allah.
Muhammad is addressed as Allah's messenger. Allah gives him spoil and lordship over whom He will, and he gives instructions that believers are told to follow.

l: the People of the Scripture, Surah 59: The Exile (Al-Hashr)
s: The People of the Scripture who disbelieved were driven from their homes in the first exile. They relied on their strongholds, were reached by Allah from where they did not expect, and ruined their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers.

The believers helped ruin the houses of the People of the Scripture and are included among those who receive guidance about spoil. Those who entered the city and faith before the fugitives loved them and preferred them above themselves, while those who came after asked forgiveness and for hearts free of rancour toward believers.
The fugitives were driven out from their homes and belongings and sought bounty from Allah and help Allah and His messenger. They are described as loyal.

The hypocrites promised their disbelieving brethren among the People of the Scripture that they would leave with them and help them, but Allah declares them liars. They neither leave with them nor help them when attacked, and they fear the believers more than Allah.
The devil is likened to one who tells man to disbelieve and then, when man disbelieves, declares that he is quit of him and fears Allah, the Lord of the Worlds.

l: the owners of the Fire, Surah 59: The Exile (Al-Hashr)
s: The owners of the Fire are not equal to the owners of the Garden. The owners of the Fire abide therein, and their consequence is presented as the reward of evil-doers.

l: the owners of the Garden, Surah 59: The Exile (Al-Hashr)
s: The owners of the Garden are not equal to the owners of the Fire. They are described as the victorious.

l: the first exile, Surah 59: The Exile (Al-Hashr)
s: The first exile was the exile in which the People of the Scripture who disbelieved were caused to go forth from their homes. Allah's reaching them and their destruction of their houses are presented as a lesson.
Allah decreed migration for the People of the Scripture concerned; without that decree, He would have punished them in the world. Their punishment in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.
The Fire is the punishment of the People of the Scripture who opposed Allah and His messenger, and the abiding consequence for the devil and the disbelieving man. The owners of the Fire abide in it.
The Garden is the destination associated with the victorious owners of the Garden, who are contrasted with the owners of the Fire.
If Allah had caused the Qur'an to descend upon a mountain, the mountain would have been seen humbled and rent asunder by fear of Allah. This similitude is given so that mankind may reflect.

Faith is shared by those who entered the city before the fugitives and by those who came after them. The later believers ask Allah to forgive their brethren who were before them in faith and to remove rancour from their hearts.
Punishment is assigned because the People of the Scripture opposed Allah and His messenger, and the hypocrites and disbelievers face painful consequences. The punishment of the Hereafter is the Fire.

Spoil given to Allah's messenger is assigned for Allah, His messenger, near of kin, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, so that it does not become a commodity among the rich. Believers are told to take what the messenger gives them and abstain from what he forbids.

l: Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana) addresses believers about relations with Allah's enemies and those who war against them on account of religion. It presents Abraham and those with him as a pattern of rejecting false worship while trusting Allah, and it permits kindness and justice toward those who do not fight or expel believers. It describes the examination and treatment of believing women who come as fugitives, and sets out conditions for women taking allegiance to the Prophet. The unit warns that kinship and children will not avail on the Day of Resurrection and refers to the Hereafter, faith, enmity, and the possibility of love between former enemies.

l: Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana), Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: It instructs believers about choosing allies, dealing with enemies and disbelievers, and showing kindness and justice to those who do not fight them. It discusses believing women who come as fugitives and the conditions of allegiance to the Prophet.

l: Allah, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Allah is described as Best Aware of what people hide and proclaim, Seer of what they do, Mighty, Forgiving, Merciful, Knower, Wise, and the Absolute, Owner of Praise. Allah forbids friendship with those who fight believers or drive them from their homes, but does not forbid kindness and justice toward others.

l: believers, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Believers are told not to choose Allah's enemies and their enemies as allies or show them secret friendship. They are instructed to trust Allah, keep their duty to Him, examine believing women, and accept the allegiance of women who meet the stated conditions.

l: Allah's enemies, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Allah's enemies are described as people who disbelieve in the truth, drive out the messenger and believers, and seek to make believers disbelieve. If they gain the upper hand, they become foes and use their hands and tongues against believers with evil intent.

l: disbelievers, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Disbelievers are described as those who oppose believers, may war against them on account of religion, and may drive them from their homes. They are also described as despairing of the Hereafter like those in the graves.

l: believing women, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Believing women may come to believers as fugitives and are to be examined regarding their faith. If they are known to be true believers, they are not to be sent back to disbelievers, and marriage to them is permitted after giving them their dues.

l: Abraham, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Abraham and those with him are presented as a goodly pattern when they declared themselves guiltless of their folk and of what they worship beside Allah. Abraham promised to ask forgiveness for his father while acknowledging that he could do nothing for him against Allah.

l: the Day of Resurrection, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: The Day of Resurrection is described as a day when ties of kindred and children will avail people nothing. Allah will part people on that day and sees what they do.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: The Hereafter is mentioned in connection with those who look to Allah and the Last Day. A folk with whom Allah is wroth are described as having despaired of the Hereafter.

l: allegiance, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Allegiance is taken by believing women who pledge not to ascribe partners to Allah, steal, commit adultery, kill their children, produce devised lies, or disobey the Prophet in what is right. The Prophet is instructed to accept their allegiance and ask Allah to forgive them.

l: enmity and hostility, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Abraham and those with him declared that hostility and hate had arisen between them and their folk until they believed in Allah only. The text also describes enmity between believers and some people who oppose them.

l: love between former enemies, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Allah may ordain love between believers and those of their enemies with whom they are at enmity. This possibility is stated alongside Allah's might and forgiveness.

l: religion, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Religion is the basis for the prohibition against friendship with those who war against believers or drive them from their homes. Those who do not fight believers on account of religion are not barred from receiving kindness and justice.

l: faith, Surah 60: She that is to be examined (Al-Mumtahana)
s: Faith is examined in believing women who come as fugitives, and Allah is described as Best Aware of their faith. Believers are told to act in accordance with belief in Allah, and women taking allegiance pledge not to ascribe partners to Him.

Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff), revealed at Medina, concerns Allah, His messengers, believers, and those who disbelieve. It condemns saying what one does not do and praises those who battle for Allah's cause in solid ranks. Moses and Jesus son of Mary are presented as messengers, and Jesus announces a messenger after him whose name is the Praised One. Believers are called to faith, striving with wealth and lives, and becoming Allah's helpers, with forgiveness, Gardens, help from Allah, and present victory promised.

l: Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff), Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: It was revealed at Medina and teaches that Allah is glorified by all in the heavens and earth. It addresses believers, messengers, striving for Allah's cause, and the opposition of disbelievers.

Allah is glorified by all in the heavens and earth, and He is the Mighty and the Wise. He loves those who battle for His cause in ranks, sends hearts astray when people go astray, guides not wrongdoing or evil-living folk, forgives sins, and strengthens believers against their foe.
Believers are told not to say what they do not do and to believe in Allah and His messenger. They should strive for Allah's cause with their wealth and lives and be Allah's helpers.
Those who battle for Allah's cause in ranks are loved by Allah. Believers are told to strive for it with their wealth and lives.
Moses asked his people why they persecuted him while knowing that he was Allah's messenger to them. When they went astray, Allah sent their hearts astray.
Moses was Allah's messenger to his people. Believers are told to believe in Allah and His messenger.

l: Jesus son of Mary, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: Jesus son of Mary said that he was Allah's messenger to the Children of Israel, confirming the Torah and bringing good tidings of a messenger after him. He asked the disciples who were his helpers for Allah.

l: Children of Israel, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: Jesus son of Mary was sent as Allah's messenger to the Children of Israel. A party of them believed and a party disbelieved.

l: the Praised One, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: The Praised One is the name of the messenger whom Jesus son of Mary announced as coming after him.
A person is summoned unto Al-Islam, but Allah does not guide wrongdoing folk.

l: the light of Allah, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: Disbelievers wish to put out the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect it despite their aversion.
Disbelievers are averse to Allah's light and to the religion of truth, and some among the Children of Israel disbelieved. They cannot put out Allah's light.

l: the religion of truth, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: Allah sent His messenger with the guidance and the religion of truth so that it may conquer all religion, despite the aversion of idolaters.
Commerce is presented as a means of salvation from a painful doom. It consists of believing in Allah and His messenger and striving for Allah's cause with wealth and lives.

l: Gardens underneath which rivers flow, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: They are promised to those who believe in Allah and His messenger and strive for Allah's cause. They are part of the forgiveness and reward offered by Allah.

l: Gardens of Eden, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: Pleasant dwellings in Gardens of Eden are promised to those who believe and strive for Allah's cause. This reward is called the supreme triumph.

l: help from Allah, Surah 61: The Ranks (As-Saff)
s: Help from Allah is promised as another blessing that believers love.
Present victory is promised as another blessing for believers, along with help from Allah.
Muhammad is addressed as the one who should give good tidings of help from Allah and present victory to believers.
Jesus son of Mary asked his disciples who were his helpers for Allah. They answered that they were Allah's helpers.

Surah 62: Friday (Al-Jumu'a), revealed at Medina, concerns Allah, His messenger, the unlettered ones, the Jews, and believers. Allah sends a messenger among the unlettered ones to recite Allah's revelations, purify them, and teach them Scripture and wisdom. The Jews are reproached for failing to apply the Law of Moses and for claiming special favor while shrinking from death. Believers are instructed to leave trading for the Friday prayer, then disperse to seek Allah's bounty and remember Allah much.

Surah 62: Friday (Al-Jumu'a) was revealed at Medina. It describes Allah's glory, the sending of a messenger among the unlettered ones, the conduct of the Jews, and instructions for believers concerning the Friday prayer.

Allah is glorified by all that is in the heavens and earth and is described as the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One, the Mighty, and the Wise. Allah sends a messenger, grants bounty, knows the visible and invisible, and is the Best of providers.
The unlettered ones receive a messenger of their own who recites Allah's revelations, makes them grow, and teaches them the Scripture and wisdom. They had previously been in manifest error.

Muhammad is addressed as the messenger who should tell the Jews that their claimed favor with Allah would require them to long for death if they were truthful. He is also told to say that the death from which they shrink will meet them.
Allah's revelations are recited by the messenger to the unlettered ones. Those who deny Allah's revelations are likened to wrongdoing folk whom Allah does not guide.
Allah's bounty is given to whom Allah wills and is described as infinite. After the Friday prayer, believers are told to seek Allah's bounty in the land.

The Jews are described as being entrusted with the Law of Moses but not applying it, like an ass carrying books. They claim to be Allah's favored people apart from mankind, yet they will never long for death because of what their hands have sent before.

The Jews shrink from death and will not long for it because of their deeds. The death from which they shrink will surely meet them, after which they will be returned to the Knower of the Invisible and the Visible.

Believers are commanded to hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave their trading when the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation. After the prayer ends, they may disperse in the land, seek Allah's bounty, and remember Allah much.

l: the call to prayer, Surah 62: Friday (Al-Jumu'a)
s: The call to prayer signals believers to hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave their trading for the prayer of the day of congregation.
The Friday prayer requires believers to leave trading when its call is heard. When it ends, they are told to disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty.
Trading is to be left when the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation. The text says this is better for believers, and after the prayer they may seek Allah's bounty.

This unit concerns the hypocrites and their claims before Muhammad, whom Allah identifies as speaking falsely despite acknowledging him as His messenger. The hypocrites use their faith as a pretext to turn people from Allah's way, resist calls for forgiveness, and seek to drive away those with Allah's messenger. They say the mightier will drive out the weaker from Medina, while Allah, His messenger, and the believers possess might. The unit also warns the believers not to let wealth or children distract them from remembrance of Allah and urges them to spend before death arrives.

Allah knows that Muhammad is His messenger and bears witness that the hypocrites speak falsely. Allah seals the hearts of those who believe and then disbelieve, will not forgive the evil-living folk, and possesses the treasures of the heavens and the earth. Allah grants no soul reprieve when its term comes and is informed of what people do.

Muhammad is Allah's messenger, and the hypocrites acknowledge this verbally while speaking falsely. He is told that asking forgiveness for them or not asking forgiveness is the same, because Allah will not forgive them.

The hypocrites come to Muhammad claiming that he is Allah's messenger, but Allah identifies their testimony as false. They use faith as a pretext to turn people from Allah's way, refuse calls to seek forgiveness, and say that the mightier will drive out the weaker from Medina. They are described as enemies, and their hearts are sealed after they believed and then disbelieved.

The believers are described as possessing might together with Allah and His messenger. They are warned not to let their wealth or children distract them from remembrance of Allah and are urged to spend from what has been provided to them before death.
The hypocrites say that if they return to Medina, the mightier will drive out the weaker.
The believers are warned not to let their wealth distract them from remembrance of Allah. They are told to spend from what Allah has provided before death comes.
The believers are warned not to let their children distract them from remembrance of Allah.

Surah 64: Mutual Disillusion concerns Allah's sovereignty, knowledge, creation, and judgment of believers and disbelievers. It warns that disbelievers denied the messengers and resurrection, while believers are urged to trust Allah, obey, spend, and guard against greed. On the Day of Assembling, believers who do right receive forgiveness and the Gardens, while those who deny the revelations face the Fire. Wives, children, wealth, and worldly temptation are described as tests, while Allah's reward is immense.

l: Surah 64: Mutual Disillusion (At-Taghaabun), Surah 64: Mutual Disillusion (At-Taghaabun)
s: The surah glorifies Allah's sovereignty, power, knowledge, and praise, and concerns belief, disbelief, resurrection, judgment, family, wealth, and reward.

Allah owns sovereignty and praise, created the heavens and the earth and shaped people, and knows what is concealed, published, and in people's breasts. He is independent, absolute, forgiving, merciful, responsive, clement, mighty, wise, and able to do all things; He guides the heart of whoever believes.

Believers are urged to believe in Allah, His messenger, and the light revealed by Allah, and to trust and obey Allah. Those who believe and do right receive forgiveness and enter the Gardens, and those saved from their own greed are successful.
Disbelievers are described as those who deny resurrection, Allah's revelations, and the messengers' clear proofs. They will be informed of what they did and will abide in the Fire.
Allah's messengers came to disbelieving peoples with clear proofs of Allah's sovereignty. Their duty is to convey the message plainly.

l: the Day of Assembling, Surah 64: Mutual Disillusion (At-Taghaabun)
s: The Day of Assembling is the day when Allah gathers people, and it is a day of mutual disillusion. On that day, believers who do right receive forgiveness and the Gardens, while disbelievers face the Fire.
Disbelievers assert that they will not be raised again, but they are told that they will be raised and informed of what they did. Their resurrection is easy for Allah.
The Gardens are granted to those who believe in Allah and do right after their evil deeds are remitted. Rivers flow underneath them, and their inhabitants abide there forever.
The Fire is the destination of those who disbelieve and deny Allah's revelations. They abide therein, and it is a hapless journey's end.
Wives may be enemies for believers, so believers are told to beware of them. If believers efface, overlook, and forgive, Allah is forgiving and merciful.
Children may be enemies for believers, so believers are told to beware of them. Believers are also told that children are a temptation.
Wealth is described as a temptation. Believers are told to spend, because spending is better for their souls.
Wives, children, and wealth are described as temptations. Believers are urged to keep their duty to Allah, listen, obey, and be saved from their own greed.
Allah's reward is immense. If people lend Allah a goodly loan, He doubles it for them and forgives them.

l: the light revealed by Allah, Surah 64: Mutual Disillusion (At-Taghaabun)
s: The light revealed by Allah is presented as something in which people are commanded to believe together with Allah and His messenger.
Those who deny Allah's revelations are owners of the Fire and abide therein. The revelations are connected with the warning delivered by the messengers.
The message is conveyed plainly by Allah's messenger, whose duty is only to deliver it. People are commanded to obey Allah and His messenger, while turning away does not alter that duty.

This unit concerns Allah's guidance to the Prophet and believers about lawful matters, repentance, protection, and conduct toward disbelievers and hypocrites. It recounts the Prophet's disclosure of a confidential matter to one of his wives and warns two wives to repent and not aid against Muhammad. It commands believers to guard themselves and their families from the Fire and promises sincere penitents Gardens with flowing rivers. It gives examples through the wives of Noah and Lot, the wife of Pharaoh, and Mary, daughter of 'Imran.

Allah is described as Forgiving, Merciful, the Protector, the Knower, and the Wise. Allah makes lawful absolution from oaths, commands repentance, promises Gardens to sincere penitents, and cites examples for believers and disbelievers.

Muhammad is identified as the one whom two wives might aid against, while Allah, Gabriel, the righteous among the believers, and the angels are his protecting friends and helpers. Muhammad is also named in connection with the Prophet's confidential disclosure to one of his wives.

l: the Prophet's wives, Surah 66: The Prohibition (At-Tahrim)
s: One of the Prophet's wives divulged a confidential fact, after which the Prophet made part of it known and passed over part. Two wives are urged to turn to Allah repentant and warned that Allah may replace them with better wives if the Prophet divorces them.

Believers are commanded to guard themselves and their families from the Fire and to turn to Allah in sincere repentance. Those who believe with the Prophet will have light running before them and on their right hands and will ask Allah to perfect their light and forgive them.

Disbelievers are told not to make excuses on the appointed day and are told that they are being paid for what they used to do. The Prophet is commanded to strive against disbelievers and hypocrites and to be stern with them.
The Fire is described as having men and stones as fuel, with strong and severe angels set over it. The wife of Noah and the wife of Lot are said to enter the Fire along with those who enter.
The Garden is promised to sincere penitents, with rivers flowing underneath. The wife of Pharaoh asks Allah to build for her a home with Him in the Garden.
Sincere repentance is commanded for believers. It may lead to the remission of evil deeds and entry into Gardens beneath which rivers flow.

l: wife of Pharaoh, Surah 66: The Prohibition (At-Tahrim)
s: The wife of Pharaoh is presented as an example for those who believe. She asks Allah for a home with Him in the Garden, deliverance from Pharaoh and his work, and deliverance from evil-doing folk.
Pharaoh is named as the husband of the believing woman who asks to be delivered from him and his work.
The Prohibition (At-Tahrim) is identified as Surah 66, revealed at Medina. This unit concerns the Prophet, his wives, believers, repentance, and examples of belief and disbelief.

This unit concerns the doom coming upon the disbelievers and Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways. It describes the Day of Judgment, when the sky becomes like molten copper, the hills like flakes of wool, and people emerge from graves in haste. The guilty man will wish to ransom himself with his family and everything on earth, but the fire of hell will seize those who turned from truth and hoarded wealth. It also describes man, worshippers, their conduct, and the Gardens promised to those who remain faithful.

l: The Ascending Stairways (Al-Ma'aarij), Surah 70: The Ascending Stairways (Al-Ma'aarij)
s: The Ascending Stairways are associated with Allah, Lord of the Ascending Stairways. The angels and the Spirit ascend unto Him by them in a Day whose span is fifty thousand years.
The doom is about to fall upon the disbelievers, and none can repel it. The doom of the Lord is such that none can feel secure before it.
The disbelievers face a doom that none can repel. They stare toward Muhammad in groups, yet they are promised a Day when they will emerge from the graves in abasement.
Allah is named as the Lord of the Ascending Stairways. He is able to replace the disbelievers with others better than them and cannot be outrun.
Muhammad is told to be patient with a patience fair to see. The disbelievers stare toward him, open-eyed, from the right and the left in groups.

l: Day of Judgment, Surah 70: The Ascending Stairways (Al-Ma'aarij)
s: The Day of Judgment is a day when the sky becomes like molten copper and the hills become like flakes of wool. People emerge from the graves in haste, with eyes aghast and abasement stupefying them.

l: guilty man, Surah 70: The Ascending Stairways (Al-Ma'aarij)
s: The guilty man will wish to ransom himself from the punishment of that day with his children, spouse, brother, kin, and all that is in the earth. The fire of hell will call him because he turned and fled from truth and hoarded wealth and withheld it.
Man was created anxious, fretful when evil befalls him, and grudging when good befalls him. Man is also described as created from what the disbelievers know.

The worshippers are constant at their worship and give an acknowledged right from their wealth to the beggar and the destitute. They believe in the Day of Judgment, fear their Lord's doom, preserve their chastity, keep pledges and covenants, stand by their testimony, and remain attentive at their worship.

l: Lord's doom, Surah 70: The Ascending Stairways (Al-Ma'aarij)
s: The Lord's doom is a punishment before which none can feel secure. Those who fear it are among the described worshippers.
The worshippers who fulfill the described qualities will dwell in Gardens, honoured.

l: Garden of Delight, Surah 70: The Ascending Stairways (Al-Ma'aarij)
s: The disbelievers hope to enter the Garden of Delight, but the text rejects this hope.

This unit concerns Noah's warning to his people and his call to serve Allah, keep their duty, and obey him. Noah says that his people resist his warnings, reject repentance, and follow leaders whose wealth and children bring ruin. He recounts Allah's signs in creation and promises of forgiveness, rain, wealth, sons, gardens, and rivers. Noah says that the people were drowned because of their sins and then entered a Fire, and he asks Allah to leave no disbelievers in the land and to forgive him, his parents, and believers.

Allah is described as the one whom Noah's people are told to serve and obey. Allah is ever Forgiving, promises rain, wealth, sons, gardens, and rivers to those who seek pardon, and is credited with creating humans, seven heavens, the moon, the sun, and the earth.

Noah warns his people of a painful doom and calls them to serve Allah, keep their duty, obey him, and seek pardon. He says that he called to them night and day, aloud, publicly, and privately, but they resisted him. Noah reports their disobedience and asks Allah to leave no disbelievers in the land and to forgive him, his parents, and believers.

Noah's people are warned to serve Allah, keep their duty, obey Noah, and seek pardon. They resist his calls, cover themselves, persist in refusal, act proudly, follow leaders, and say not to forsake their gods. They are described as disobeying Noah and leading others astray.
Noah's people are told not to forsake their gods, including Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. Their devotion to these gods is presented as part of the people's rejection of Noah's warning.
The wrong-doers are said to be increased in error. Noah asks Allah not to increase them in anything except ruin.
The disbelievers are drowned because of their sins. After drowning, they are made to enter a Fire and find no helpers in place of Allah.
The Fire is the punishment into which the disbelievers are made to enter after they are drowned because of their sins. They find no helpers in place of Allah.

The unit concerns Muhammad, the Jinn, humankind, and Allah. The Jinn hear the Qur'an, believe in its guidance, affirm Allah's uniqueness, and describe their different groups and accountability. Muhammad is instructed to say that he prays only to Allah, controls neither harm nor benefit, and conveys the Truth and Allah's messages. The unit warns of hell for those who disobey and describes the promised event, whose timing is known only to Allah.

Muhammad receives the revelation that a company of the Jinn heard the Qur'an. He is instructed to say that he prays only to Allah, ascribes no partner to Him, controls neither harm nor benefit, and conveys the Truth and Allah's messages.

Allah is described as the Lord of the Jinn, exalted above having a wife or son. He alone is invoked, knows the Unseen, reveals His secret to chosen messengers, guards their conveyance of His messages, surrounds all doings, and keeps count of all things.

The Jinn hear a marvellous Qur'an, believe in it, and affirm that Allah has no partner. They include righteous and unrighteous groups, some surrendered to Allah, and they acknowledge that they cannot escape Him.

Humankind is mentioned as having been thought by the Jinn to speak no lie concerning Allah. Individuals of humankind used to invoke the protection of individuals of the Jinn, increasing them in revolt against Allah.
The Qur'an is heard by a company of the Jinn, who call it marvellous and say that it guides unto righteousness. Hearing its guidance leads them to believe.
The Jinn sought heaven but found it filled with strong warders and meteors. They used to sit in places therein to listen, but whoever listens now finds a flame waiting for him.
The Jinn do not know whether harm is intended for all who are in the earth or whether Allah intends guidance for them. They state that they cannot escape from Allah in the earth.
The unjust among the Jinn have not surrendered to Allah and are described as firewood for hell.

l: the right path, Surah 72: The Jinn (Al-Jinn)
s: Those among the Jinn who surrender to Allah have taken the right path purposefully. If the idolaters tread the right path, Allah says He will give them water in abundance as a test.

l: places of worship, Surah 72: The Jinn (Al-Jinn)
s: The places of worship are only for Allah. Therefore, prayer is not to be directed to anyone along with Allah.
The Truth is conveyed by Muhammad as part of his duty from Allah.
Muhammad conveys Allah's messages. Allah places a guard before and behind His chosen messenger so that it is known that the messages have been conveyed.
Those who disobey Allah and His messenger have the fire of hell, where they dwell forever. The unjust are described as firewood for hell.

l: the promised event, Surah 72: The Jinn (Al-Jinn)
s: The promised event is something the disbelievers may doubt until they behold it. Muhammad does not know whether it is near or whether Allah has appointed a distant term for it.

Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil) concerns commands to the enshrouded one concerning night vigil, recitation, remembrance, devotion, patience, and reliance on Allah. It warns of punishment for deniers and recalls Pharaoh's rebellion against a messenger. It presents the coming day when the earth and hills quake and the heaven is rent asunder. It concludes by easing the requirement of night vigil and instructing recitation, worship, almsgiving, good works, and seeking forgiveness.

l: Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil), Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil)
s: Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil) was revealed at Mecca. It contains commands concerning vigil, recitation, devotion, patience, and worship, along with warnings of punishment and guidance toward Allah's forgiveness.

l: the Prophet (the enshrouded one), Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil)
s: The enshrouded one is commanded to keep vigil during the night, chant the Qur'an in measure, remember Allah's name, devote himself completely, choose Allah as his defender, and bear patiently what others utter. He is told to recite what is easy, establish worship, pay the poor-due, lend to Allah a goodly loan, and seek forgiveness.

Allah is identified as the Lord of the East and the West, with no Allah save Him, and as the one who measures the night and the day. Allah turns in mercy, knows the conditions of the sick, travelers, and those fighting for His cause, and is Forgiving and Merciful.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil)
s: The Qur'an is to be chanted in measure during the night vigil. The enshrouded one and those with him are instructed to recite of it what is easy for them.

l: the messenger (sent unto you), Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil)
s: A messenger has been sent unto the people as a witness against them, just as a messenger was sent unto Pharaoh. Pharaoh rebelled against the messenger, and Allah seized him with no gentle grip.

l: the night, Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil)
s: The night is described as a time when impression is more keen and speech more certain. The enshrouded one and some of those with him keep vigil for nearly two-thirds of it, or half or a third, while Allah measures the night and the day.

l: the Reminder, Surah 73: The Enshrouded One (Al-Muzzammil)
s: The passage identifies itself as a Reminder. Whoever wills is told to choose a way unto his Lord.

Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir) concerns the addressed prophet, who is commanded to rise, warn, magnify his Lord, purify his raiment, shun pollution, and remain patient. It describes the man created by Allah who rejects Allah's revelations and is threatened with the burning. It explains that the Fire has nineteen angelic wardens and presents this number as a test for believers, those given Scripture, and disbelievers. The unit warns men about the Hereafter, the Day of Judgment, and the consequences awaiting the guilty, while calling whoever wills to heed the Reminder.

l: Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir), Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: It commands the addressed prophet to arise and warn, magnify his Lord, purify his raiment, shun pollution, and be patient for the sake of his Lord. It warns of the trumpet, the Fire, the guilty, and the Day of Judgment, and calls whoever wills to heed the Reminder.
Allah is to be magnified by the addressed prophet. Allah appoints angels as wardens of the Fire, guides or sends astray whom He wills, and is the fount of fear and Mercy.

l: the addressed prophet, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The addressed prophet is told to arise and warn, magnify his Lord, purify his raiment, shun pollution, avoid showing favour for worldly gain, and be patient for the sake of his Lord.

l: the man created by Allah, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The man created by Allah is described as having been given ample means, sons abiding in his presence, and a smooth life, yet desiring more. He is stubborn toward Allah's revelations, plans against them, calls them magic and mortal speech, and is threatened with the burning.

Disbelievers will face a day of anguish rather than ease. They may stumble over the number of the Fire's wardens, ask what Allah means by the similitude, deny the Hereafter, and be punished in the burning.
Angels are appointed as wardens of the Fire, whose number is nineteen.
Men are warned by the signs of the Moon, the withdrawing night, and the shining dawn. Each person may advance or hang back, and whoever wills may heed the Reminder.

l: the guilty, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The guilty will be questioned in gardens about what brought them to the burning. They will say that they did not pray or feed the wretched, disputed vainly, and denied the Day of Judgment until the Inevitable came.

l: the Fire, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The Fire has nineteen angelic wardens. It leaves nothing, spares nothing, and shrivels the man.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The Hereafter is feared by some who deny it, and those who do not fear it turn away from the Admonishment. The unit presents it as the realm whose consequences the guilty will face.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The Day of Judgment is denied by the guilty until the Inevitable comes to them. On that occasion, the mediation of no mediators will avail them.

l: the trumpet sounding, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: When the trumpet shall sound, that day will be a day of anguish and not of ease for disbelievers.

l: Allah's revelations, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The man created by Allah is stubborn toward Allah's revelations. He dismisses them as magic from of old and as the speech of a mortal man.

l: the Reminder, Surah 74: The Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir)
s: The number of the Fire's wardens is described as a Reminder unto mortals. The unit calls it an Admonishment and says that whoever wills may heed it.

Surah 75: The Resurrection (Al-Qiyaama) concerns the Day of Resurrection, the resurrection of the dead, and the fate of man. It describes the cosmic signs of that day, including confused sight, an eclipsed moon, and the joining of the sun and moon. Man will be shown what he sent before and left behind, while some faces will be resplendent and others despondent. The unit also warns that man will face death and be brought before his Lord, who is able to restore him after death.
